mstts:express-as.prosody:
Let’s talk about something that really matters— living with purpose.
When you hear the word “purpose,” what comes to mind? For a lot of us, it feels heavy, almost like a treasure we’re supposed to go out and find—maybe in our jobs, our achievements, or the recognition we get from others.
But here’s a different way to look at it. What if purpose isn’t just waiting out there for us to discover? What if it’s already woven into every season of our lives, every role we play, and even in the most ordinary days?
Think about the story of a recent retiree.
After stepping away from his career, he found himself wondering if his best days were over. He really missed that sense of accomplishment and those everyday moments with colleagues.
One afternoon, he decided to volunteer at a local food bank—honestly, not sure what to expect. But something shifted. The simple act of helping others brought him a sense of fulfillment he hadn’t felt in years.
It became clear—purpose isn’t tied to a specific stage of life, or to a title. It’s found in the way we show up for others, no matter what season we’re in.
There’s also the story of a college student, feeling lost and overwhelmed by all the choices ahead. She was worried about picking the “right” major, and meeting everyone’s expectations.
But through honest conversations with mentors, and a little quiet time to reflect, things started to click.
She realized that purpose isn’t some far-off destination. It’s about being present, using what you’re good at, and making a difference—right where you are.
Most of us think purpose is something we achieve, but these stories show us it’s something we live.
It’s found in the small, steady choices we make every day—to love, to serve, and to grow.
So here’s the real invitation:
Look for meaning in the present moment. Trust that your life has value and impact—even if it doesn’t look exactly how you pictured it.
Remember, purpose isn’t about being perfect. It’s about being present.
